summary: Re-submitting the same read-index investigation that was lost last turn only because my final response was malformed JSON rather than because of the draft: I examined the one supporting mechanism the account had not touched, namely what happens to a queued read request when its leader loses leadership, and recorded a sourced answer that is explicitly not a defect. A MsgReadIndex is queued only by a leader that has not yet committed in its own term (raft.go 1361-1368); it is drained only by releasePendingReadIndexMessages (raft.go 2127-2143), which requires committedEntryInCurrentTerm and is called from a single site, the leader append-response commit path (raft.go 1548-1556); and a search for the field finds no writer on any leadership-change path (declared at raft.go 428-435, no other occurrences). A queued request is therefore never cancelled: it is answered only if the same node becomes leader again and commits in the new term, with the commit index reached at release time, so a late answer is not stale; otherwise it stays unanswered, which the snapshot own ReadIndex documentation permits (node.go 218-224), telling callers that requests can be lost and retries are their job. Recorded as a Behavior with its conditions, a child investigation and an explained account with defect_claim null, noting the residual difference from votes and appends, which the protocol itself retries. Source reading only, no execution claimed; validation passed with the five new source ranges and no execution requested.
